Santa Ana Pueblo

Santa Ana Pueblo, called Tamaya in its own publications, is a distinct New Mexico Pueblo. Its preservation and education departments provide starting points into community-guided heritage work, Keres learning and support across generations.

01

Identity and context

Santa Ana Pueblo, also known as Tamaya, is a living Pueblo nation in New Mexico.

Read the sources [1] Santa Ana Pueblo

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Community-preferred naming, Keres language context and Pueblo-authored history. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Santa Ana Pueblo [2] Santa Ana Pueblo [3] wiki.ubc.ca

03

Preserving Tamaya’s past for the future

Santa Ana’s THPO dates its creation to 2011 and describes guidance from an advisory board of community cultural authorities. Public work includes preservation education and protecting historical documents. The account outlines responsibilities while leaving private knowledge and individual cultural places outside this guide.

Read the sources [1] Santa Ana Pueblo

04

Education across community life

The Education Department describes early learning with Keres classes, school-family liaison work, scholarships and a community library. Its after-school and summer programmes combine academic support, creative activities and language/culture learning. These are the Pueblo’s service descriptions rather than an evaluation of participation or outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Santa Ana Pueblo
